name: g6_protocol
label: DESCRIPTIVE PROFILING (no decision rule)
requested_for: Manuscript A (cost / latency section); PI-approved G6

bases: tkgl-polecat TiRGN (hardening checkpoint, valid-best epoch; authors' model code via the project's pure-torch DGL shim)
systems.optional: tkgl-icews RE-GCN (Stage B) only if its frozen checkpoint and pipeline inputs are already on <HOST> and the extra cost is < 1 h; otherwise reported as not run

arms.base: frozen base alone (score row -> ranked answer list)
arms.HR: history re-ranker over base top-50 (19 features, W = 50)
arms.HRCOV_PAT: bridge-free HRCOV: base top-50 ++ first <= 50 pattern-prior candidates (W = 100), 25 features

stages.S1_base_scoring: frozen base produces the full log-prob row for the query (online ground-truth history < t); the per-snapshot history update / evolution that all queries of a timestamp share is timed separately and also reported amortised per query
stages.S2_candidate_generation: top-50 of the base row (HR, HRCOV_PAT) + the pattern-prior block (HRCOV_PAT only; 1-2-hop entity-anonymised path patterns over the online event index, pilot-1 setting)
stages.S3_feature_extraction: the re-ranker features of every candidate (8 base + 11 evidence for HR; + 6 pattern-coverage for HRCOV_PAT)
stages.S4_rerank_fusion: re-ranker MLP inference (seed-0 trained model) + fusion alpha*log p + beta*f + final ordering

sample: fixed 10,000-query sample of the test split of each dataset (numpy default_rng(0) choice without replacement over test query indices in harness split order, then sorted by timestamp so history is processed online); identical sample for all arms

modes.batch_1: queries one at a time (per-query wall-clock, torch.cuda.synchronize around GPU stages)
modes.batched: all sample queries of one timestamp together (GPU stages chunked at 512); per-query latency = batch time / batch size

repeats: 3 timed repeats after 1 warm-up pass (warm cache: data loaded, indices built, CUDA kernels compiled); per-query latency statistics pooled over repeats
metrics: per-query latency p50 / p95 / mean per stage and end-to-end, batch-1 and batched (ms)
throughput (queries / s) per arm and mode
peak GPU memory per stage (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated, reset per stage) and process peak (nvidia-smi sampled)
peak host RSS per stage (resource / psutil)
amortised overhead vs base alone = (arm end-to-end time - base time) / base time, per mode
one-off setup costs reported separately (index build, model load), not included in per-query latency
environment: <HOST>, GPU 1 only (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB; GPU 0 is busy with G8 and is not touched), tkg-gpu:latest (torch 2.8.0+cu128); CPU stages single-process (no worker pool) with a fixed thread count; host / GPU / driver / CUDA / torch / numpy / scipy versions and concurrent load (other jobs on the host) recorded
caveats_to_report: the host is shared (G8 training on GPU 0 and its CPU retrieval workers run concurrently), so absolute latencies are upper bounds for a dedicated machine; the pipeline code is research code (python loops), not an optimised serving implementation
